true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Raw HTML imports bypass sanitization and enable stored XSS

Returning `raw` directly makes imported HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed content to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; neither step removes scripts, event handlers, or unsafe link schemes. Furthermore, `TopicEmbed.import` interpolates the source URL into HTML without escaping it, allowing quotes in a fetched URL's query to inject attributes into the attribution link. These posts are subsequently rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Sanitize imported HTML, escape the attribution URL, and retain sanitization when raw-HTML posts are edited.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB closing statement prevents discussion rendering

The conditional ends with `end if` instead of `end`. This generates invalid Ruby when Rails compiles the template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail rather than display the discussion. The controller specs do not render views and therefore miss this failure. Replace the closing statement and add a view-rendering test.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed polling assumes every entry has an Atom content field

Valid RSS entries commonly provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. SimpleRSS exposes these separately, so `i.content` can be nil and calling `scrub` raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire polling run and also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback. Select the available body field and handle entries without content; cover an actual RSS feed in the tests.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus imports no longer preserve thread creation dates

The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title. TopicEmbed creates the topic and initial post with the current time, while imported replies still use their historical dates. This loses the original thread timestamps and can leave replies dated before the topic's initial post. Pass the exported creation time through the import helpers to PostCreator.

URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths

The leading-slash check treats `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as a path on the article's host, rewriting it to something like `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Conversely, document-relative URLs such as `images/image.jpg` are left unchanged and resolve against the forum instead of the source article. The same problem exists in the image branch below. Resolve references against the complete source URL using URI resolution rather than concatenating a host prefix.

Consequently, a sync response containing access_token, expires_in, and refresh_token loses its expiry and refresh token. Authenticate outbound credential-sync requests

The request asks the parent platform to return a user's access token using only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no authentication header or signature. The configured webhook secret is checked only on inbound requests. A normally authenticated parent endpoint will reject these requests; accepting them as implemented would expose users' third-party access tokens to anyone who can reach that endpoint and enumerate IDs. Include a configured authentication mechanism in the outbound request.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing revoked credentials

The update path replaces only the key. Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after an invalid_grant response, so syncing fresh credentials after a user reconnects on the parent platform leaves the existing record marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the integration. Reset invalid to false when accepting replacement credentials.

Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce client

The new credential update references `prisma`, but this file never imports or declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if emitted anyway, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

Send the actual Zoom app slug to the sync endpoint

This sends `zoomvideo` as appSlug, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and the webhook identifies apps by their stored slug. A parent platform using the same app identifiers for ingestion and refresh cannot resolve this request. Use `zoom` rather than the integration directory name.

Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The cache-deletion success handler only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards an optional onChanged callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so without a caller-provided refetch the UI continues displaying the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action after reporting success. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve cache status for in-memory delegation credentials

Connected calendars can contain in-memory delegation credentials with negative IDs, whereas CalendarCache rows reference persisted credentials. Looking up status solely by the displayed credentialId therefore returns no cache for these connections, even when availability is being served from cached data. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles this case through userId and the calendar key, including reuse of pre-delegation cache rows. Resolve the corresponding persisted cache records for delegated connections as well; otherwise these users cannot see or clear their active cache through the new UI.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script location

ENV_FILE is relative to the caller's working directory, not the script directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, while leaving the application's environment unchanged. Derive the repository root from BASH_SOURCE before selecting .env so the advertised webhook configuration is actually applied.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The process type check skips killing spawned workers

Workers are created using multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These inherit from BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is therefore left running while a replacement is started for the same shards. This leaks workers and allows the old worker to resume flushing concurrently with its replacement. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from processes before killing the worker.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not skip remaining workers when the join deadline expires

Once the shared deadline expires, this break bypasses cleanup for every remaining worker. This happens if next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher uses the remaining time. Setting stopped does not interrupt a worker blocked on Redis or a Kafka future, so those workers can survive a rebalance and continue operating on shards assigned to new workers. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, and still terminate all surviving processes before returning.

If the count is one below the limit, two requests for different new device IDs can both observe available capacity and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana replicas sharing a database. Those excess devices then remain eligible for updates even after the limit is reached.
